newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Right-wing Portuguese party urges EMU vote.
newsitem.headline: Right-wing Portuguese party urges EMU vote.

text.p: Portugal's right-wing Popular Party launched on Tuesday a campaign for a referendum on whether to join the European Union's planned single currency.

"If the single currency is a good thing for Portugal, then let us explain to the Portuguese its benefits so that they can decide," party leader Manuel Monteiro told a news conference in this northern city.
He said the party had started collecting signatures in favour of a reform of the constitution to allow referenda to be held.

Portugal's ruling Socialist Party and its main Social Democrat opposition, which together hold 75 percent of the seats in parliament, strongly support Portugal's entry to Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the single currency's launch in 1999.

Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has ruled out any referendum on the Maastricht Treaty, the blueprint for monetary union, saying that even if the constitution were changed a ballot could not be used to revoke existing international commitments.
The Popular Party can only look to the Communists, who share its opposition to monetary union, for potential support. The two parties have 15 seats each in the 230-seat parliament.
Monteiro said Portugal was not in condition to bear the "social and economic" costs implied by the surrender of the escudo and its replacement by the proposed European currency.
